Logistics and inventory · Start · Tested
In 1 minute

Slow-moving inventory review

Arthur · Inventory Analyst

A building materials chain with 12 stores and one distribution center has 38 thousand active SKUs, and the stock report has 40 thousand lines that nobody reads in full.

When it runs
First business day of each month, after the stock position report with last movement is closed; the inventory analyst attaches the report to the conversation with the agent.
What it delivers in production
A monthly list by category of slow-moving and obsolete items, with days without a sale, value at cost, item master status and the disposition suggested by the category rule, sent to each buyer on the first business day.
Who decides
Lists only; the buyer decides the disposition
Effort
Calibrate on 3 past months; 3 reviewed months
Set up5 steps · 6 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# IDENTITY
You are the slow-moving and obsolete stock Human AI. You classify items by time without a sale and suggest a disposition using the category rule. You do not change stock, prices or transfers.

# CONTEXT
Building materials chain with 12 stores and one DC, 38 thousand active SKUs. The turnover policy and disposition rules by category are in turnover_disposition_policy.md, attached.

Show content
# Turnover and disposition policy by category

The position date is the base date of the run. Days without a sale = position date minus the line's last_sale.

## Before classifying
- Receipt in the last 60 days: off the list, a recent purchase is not lack of turnover.
- mandatory_replenishment = yes: off the list, flagged as mandatory replenishment.
- Expiry within 60 days of the position: EXPIRY block, with the value of the lines.

## Bands and disposition by category
| Category | Start of 1st band | 1st band (up to 180) | 181 to 365 | Above 365 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tiles | 90 days | endcap display | 20% promotion | consolidate at the DC and clearance promotion |
| Electrical | 120 days | bundle with a fast-moving item | 15% promotion | clearance promotion |
| Hardware | 90 days | endcap display | return to supplier | return to supplier |
| Paints | 90 days | endcap display | 20% promotion | clearance promotion |
| Fixtures | 90 days | endcap display | 15% promotion | clearance promotion |
| Mortars | 90 days | endcap display | 20% promotion | write-off as loss, buyer's decision |
| Heating | seasonal, season from May to August | | | |

- A seasonal item out of season is not classified: it appears as SEASONAL, with no band.
- Return to supplier only in Hardware (clause 7.2 of the supply contract).
- Idle line of a SKU that sold at another location in the last 90 days: the disposition is a transfer to that location, never a promotion.

## Rules with no leeway
- The band applies per line (SKU and location). E.g.: 118210 at Store 02 has gone 506 days without a sale and falls above 365; Store 03 sold it 22 days ago, so the disposition is transfer to Store 03.
- Electrical starts at 120 days. E.g.: 130077 with 111 days is not slow-moving; 130120 with 167 days falls in the 1st band.
- Empty last_receipt field: the line is not classified and goes to INCOMPLETE DATA. E.g.: 170015.
- An identical repeated line counts once, in value and in counts. E.g.: 160200 at Store 03.
- Percentage of stock = slow-moving value divided by the value of all lines in the position, without the repeated one. E.g.: R$ 137,316 of R$ 196,766 = 69.8%.
- In the table by band, the SKU counts in each band where it has a line; in the header, it counts once. E.g.: 112090 falls above 365 (Store 01) and in 181 to 365 (Store 02), and is 1 of the 8 slow-moving SKUs.
- Item value for escalation = sum of the SKU's lines above 365 days. Every tier that applies counts. E.g.: 112044 adds up to R$ 70,500 and goes to the commercial manager and to controllership; the expiry block goes to the buyer with the commercial manager.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Step 5 of 5 · Use

Replace the sample with your data

Do this
  1. 1Remove the sample from Input and delete it from the trash too: the connector reads files in the trash
  2. 2Replace the sample in the knowledge base with your company's text
  3. 3On the first business day of the month, export from the ERP the position with last sale and last receipt, the 12-month sales and the item master to the Input folder and click ▶
  4. 4Replace the policy in the knowledge base with your chain's: band start by category, season of seasonal items, dispositions and the categories with a return clause
  5. 5After 2 months with the buyers checking the list, connect Google Sheets to record each item's disposition; write-offs and transfers stay in the ERP, done by the buyer

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not write off stock, change prices or create transfers; the disposition decision belongs to the buyer, and so does the execution in the ERP. An item with a receipt in the last 60 days stays off the list even with no sales, because a recent purchase is not a lack of turnover. A replacement item or warranty part kept by manufacturer obligation appears flagged and outside the write-off suggestion. A return to the supplier is suggested only when the supply contract includes that clause.

Common mistakes

  • Classifying as slow-moving an item that just came into stock, because the report only looks at the last sale.
  • Adding up stock across the 12 stores when the item sells well in 2 and sits idle in the other 10, which is a transfer case, not a promotion case.
  • Treating a seasonal item, such as a heater in February, with the same day cutoff as continuously selling items.
  • Suggesting a return to the supplier without checking whether the contract has the clause.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Time to build the slow-moving items list by categoryfrom a quarter's worth of memory to a 30-minute monthly readestimate based on the described routine
Value of stock with no sale in more than 365 daystracked month by month in the spreadsheet, with a target set by the sales managerestimate based on the described routine
Items close to expiry identified before they expirefrom discovery on the shelf to a monthly list 60 days in advanceestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Position of 08/31, 38,240 SKUs read, 2,960 with no sale in more than 90 days, value at cost R$ 4.18 million (3.4% of stock).

Wall and floor tiles category, items above 365 days, top 3: 112044 Beige porcelain tile 80x80, 412 m² across 3 stores, R$ 38,900, discontinued by the supplier in 2025, suggested disposition: consolidate at the DC and promote; 118210 Blue glass mosaic, 96 boxes, R$ 12,100, active, disposition: transfer to store 07, the only one that sold it this year; 110932 Ceramic floor tile 45x45, 1,080 m², R$ 21,600, active, last receipt 40 days ago, disposition: do not act, recent purchase.
Attention, expiry: 26 SKUs of mortar and grout expire within 60 days, R$ 34,000, listed separately for immediate promotion.
